en: The Hymn to the Auspicious Mother of the World (Śrījagadambikāstotra)
I bow to that Great Power (Mahāśakti), who, accompanied by the powers such as Aindrī and others, conquered the demon Mahiṣāsura, and who is pleased by the recitation of the seed-syllable "Hrīṃ. ||1||
I bow to the Goddess in the form of the seed-syllable *klīṃ*, the destroyer of the enemies of the gods, Cāmuṇḍā, the subduer of skulls, who dwells in Tulajāpura. ||2||

I bow to the one of great intellect, whose body is adorned with a garland of skulls, who dispels the blinding darkness of delusion, and who destroys the suffering caused by ḍākinīs and other malevolent beings. 3.
Those by whom this was sung repeatedly attained all their goals;
from it, men quickly obtain both discernment and perpetual dispassion. ||4||
I worship that which exists in all beings in the form of consciousness;
be gracious, O Goddess, and always forgive my transgressions. (5)
Thus ends the Śrījagadambikāstotra composed by Śrī Vāsudevānandasarasvatī, a disciple of Śrī Pādukāpāda.
